newsitem.title: USA: Mass. selects official state chocolate chip cookie.
newsitem.headline: Mass. selects official state chocolate chip cookie.

text.p: Gov. William Weld, crumbling before political pressure, signed a bill Wednesday making the tollhouse cookie Massachussetts' official chocolate chip cookie.
Surrounded by children -- and dozens of cookies -- at a State House news conference, Weld said he would introduce a new measure to make Nabisco's Fig Newton the state's official fruit cookie.
"I don't think any other state has a fruit cookie. This is another respect for which Massachusetts is going to lead the nation," Weld said in signing the bill.
The tollhouse cookie was invented in 1930 by a woman at the Toll House Restaurant in Whitman, Mass., who ran out of cocoa while baking chocolate cookies.

As part of their political science education, Whitman students helped draft the bill making the tasty treat an official state symbol. The legislature, after much debate and over the opposition of Fig Newton fans, passed the measure earlier this month.
"When this was being debated, Gov. Weld threw his weight, which is considerable, behind the Fig Newton," said his deputy press secretary, Ilene Hoffer.
The Nabisco company invented the Fig Newton in Newton, Mass., in 1891.
